title: How to Boil and Peel an Egg Cleanly
body:
Cook eggs all the way through with a tender yolk and peel the shell off in big pieces instead of little chips.

Skill level: First-timer · Time needed: 15 minutes

Tools and materials

  • Pot with a lid
  • Eggs
  • Bowl
  • Ice
  • Spoon

Steps

  1. Put the eggs in the pot in a single layer so they do not stack or bang together.
  2. Cover the eggs with cold water by about two and a half centimetres.
  3. Put the pot on high heat and bring the water to a full rolling boil.
  4. As soon as it boils, put the lid on, turn the heat off, and leave the pot alone for ten minutes for large eggs.
  5. Move the eggs into a bowl of ice water and leave them for five minutes.
  6. Crack each egg all over on the counter, roll it gently, then peel under running water starting from the wide end.

Common mistakes

  • Boiling hard the whole time, which makes rubbery whites and a green ring around the yolk.
  • Skipping the ice bath, which makes the shell cling.
  • Trying to peel while the egg is still hot.

Troubleshooting

  • The shell sticks in chips: Peel under running water and use eggs that are a few days old, since very fresh eggs peel worse.
  • A green ring appears around the yolk: Shorten the resting time by a minute or two next time and cool the eggs faster.

Safety

The pot and water are very hot. Use oven mitts and keep children back from the stove.

What to try next

Turn the peeled eggs into egg salad or deviled eggs.

title: How to Open a Stuck Jar Lid
body:
Break the vacuum seal on a jar that will not twist open, without hurting your hands or breaking the glass.

Skill level: First-timer · Time needed: 5 minutes

Tools and materials

  • Towel or rubber grip
  • Rubber band
  • Spoon handle
  • Hot water

Steps

  1. Dry the jar and lid so your hands do not slip.
  2. Tap firmly all around the edge of the lid with a spoon handle to loosen the seal.
  3. Run hot water over just the lid for about thirty seconds so the metal expands slightly.
  4. Wrap a towel or rubber band around the lid for grip.
  5. Twist counter-clockwise with steady pressure, not a sudden jerk.
  6. If it still will not move, repeat the hot water and tapping once more.

Common mistakes

  • Forcing the lid with bare hands until your hands hurt.
  • Prying with a knife, which can slip and cut you or chip the glass.

Troubleshooting

  • The lid still will not move: Repeat the hot-water step and tap again; two rounds usually do it.
  • Your hands keep slipping: Use a dry rubber grip and make sure the lid is dry too.

Safety

Glass can break if forced. If the jar is chipped or cracked, throw it away instead of forcing the lid.

What to try next

Open a jar with a safety button lid and listen for the pop that means the seal broke.

title: How to Fold a Fitted Sheet
body:
Turn a stretchy fitted sheet with elastic corners into a flat, neat rectangle that stacks nicely.

Skill level: First-timer · Time needed: 5 minutes

Tools and materials

  • A flat surface such as a bed or table

Steps

  1. Hold the sheet lengthwise with one hand inside each top corner, elastic side facing you.
  2. Bring your hands together and tuck one corner inside the other so both corners sit on one hand.
  3. Pick up the bottom corners the same way and tuck them into the top corners.
  4. Lay the sheet flat; it should now look like a rectangle with elastic gathered along one edge.
  5. Fold that elastic edge inward so the rectangle has straight sides.
  6. Fold the rectangle in thirds, smooth it flat, and stack it.

Common mistakes

  • Balling the sheet up instead of folding, which wrinkles it and wastes space.
  • Skipping the corner tuck, which leaves lumps that will not lie flat.

Troubleshooting

  • The elastic corners keep popping out: Re-tuck each corner before every fold instead of trying to hold them all at once.
  • The folded sheet looks lumpy: Lay it flat and smooth it with your hands after each fold.

Safety

No safety hazards. This is a light, safe task.

What to try next

Fold a duvet cover the same way, matching its corners first.

title: How to Remove Sticker Residue
body:
Get the sticky leftover film off a surface after peeling a sticker, without scratching or staining it.

Skill level: First-timer · Time needed: 10 minutes

Tools and materials

  • Warm soapy water
  • Soft cloth
  • Cooking oil or peanut butter
  • Plastic scraper or old card

Steps

  1. Peel off as much of the sticker as you can with your fingers.
  2. Wash the area with warm soapy water and dry it.
  3. Rub a thin layer of cooking oil or peanut butter over the sticky residue.
  4. Wait five minutes so the oil softens the glue.
  5. Scrape gently with a plastic scraper or old card, working from one edge.
  6. Wash again with warm soapy water to remove the oil.

Common mistakes

  • Scraping with a metal blade on plastic, which scratches it.
  • Using strong solvents on plastic or painted surfaces, which can melt or discolour them.

Troubleshooting

  • Sticky film remains: Repeat the oil and wait step once more before scraping again.
  • The surface looks cloudy: Wash with warm soapy water and dry with a soft cloth; test any cleaner on a hidden spot first.

Safety

Keep solvents away from flames and test any cleaner on a hidden spot first.

What to try next

Remove a price tag from a glass jar using the same method.

title: How to Address an Envelope Correctly
body:
Write an address on an envelope so it reaches the right person without delay or return.

Skill level: First-timer · Time needed: 5 minutes

Tools and materials

  • Envelope
  • Pen
  • The full address
  • Stamp

Steps

  1. Write the recipient's full name in the centre of the envelope.
  2. Write the street address on the next line, including the house number.
  3. Write the city, state or region, and postal code on the next line.
  4. Write your own name and return address in the top left corner.
  5. Stick the stamp in the top right corner.
  6. Read everything back once to check spelling, house number, and postal code.

Common mistakes

  • Leaving out the postal code, which slows delivery.
  • Leaving out the return address, so an undeliverable letter cannot come back to you.

Troubleshooting

  • You are unsure of the postal code: Check the postal directory before writing, rather than guessing.
  • You wrote the wrong address: Use a fresh envelope; crossed-out addresses can confuse sorting.

Safety

No safety hazards. Never send cash or original documents you cannot replace.

title: How to Ripen an Avocado
body:
Take a hard avocado to perfectly ripe in a few days, and know exactly when it is ready to eat.

Skill level: First-timer · Time needed: 2 to 4 days of waiting, 2 minutes of work

Tools and materials

  • Paper bag
  • A banana or apple (optional)
  • Kitchen counter

Steps

  1. Press the avocado gently with your palm, not your fingertips; a hard one is unripe.
  2. Put the avocado in a paper bag and fold the top closed.
  3. Add a banana or apple to the bag if you want it to ripen faster.
  4. Leave the bag on the counter at room temperature.
  5. Check once a day by pressing gently with your palm.
  6. When it yields slightly to gentle pressure, it is ripe; use it now or refrigerate it to hold it for a day or two.

Common mistakes

  • Putting a hard avocado in the fridge, where it may never ripen properly.
  • Microwaving a hard avocado, which cooks it unevenly instead of ripening it.

Troubleshooting

  • It is still hard after days: Keep it in the bag with the banana and check again tomorrow.
  • It went overripe: Use it for dressing or a smoothie, where soft texture does not matter.

Safety

Cut away from your hand when opening an avocado, with the knife moving away from your body.

What to try next

title: How to Clean Eyeglasses Without Scratching Them
body:
Wash glasses so the lenses are clear and the coatings stay undamaged.

Skill level: First-timer · Time needed: 5 minutes

Tools and materials

  • Lukewarm water
  • A drop of dish soap
  • Microfibre cloth

Steps

  1. Rinse both lenses under lukewarm running water to wash off dust and grit.
  2. Put one tiny drop of dish soap on each lens.
  3. Lather gently with your fingertips, including the frame edges and nose pads.
  4. Rinse again under lukewarm water until the soap is gone.
  5. Shake off the water gently.
  6. Dry with a clean microfibre cloth, holding the glasses by the frame edge.

Common mistakes

  • Wiping dusty lenses dry, which drags grit across the lens and scratches it.
  • Drying with a shirt hem or towel, which can carry grit.
  • Using very hot water, which can damage lens coatings.

Troubleshooting

  • Smears remain after drying: Wash again properly instead of rubbing harder with the cloth.
  • A screw feels loose: Have it tightened by an optician rather than forcing it.

Safety

Do not use cleaners containing ammonia on coated lenses unless the maker says they are safe.

title: How to Hang a Picture Straight
body:
Hang a framed picture at the right height, level, and secure on the wall.

Skill level: Beginner · Time needed: 20 minutes

Tools and materials

  • Hammer
  • Picture hook or nail
  • Pencil
  • Tape measure
  • Level

Steps

  1. Choose the spot and mark the centre of the frame at about eye level, roughly 145 centimetres from the floor.
  2. Measure how far below the top of the frame the wire or hanger sits when pulled tight.
  3. Add that distance to your centre mark to find where the hook should go, and mark it with a pencil.
  4. Hammer the picture hook into the mark, keeping your fingers clear.
  5. Hang the frame on the hook.
  6. Check with the level and nudge one side until the bubble sits centred.

Common mistakes

  • Guessing the height by eye, which usually ends up too high.
  • Using a nail that is too small for a heavy frame.

Troubleshooting

  • The picture hangs crooked: Lift one side slightly and re-seat it on the hook, then level-check again.
  • The frame is heavy: Use two hooks spread apart, or fix into a wall stud.

Safety

Check for hidden wires and pipes before hammering, and never hammer close to an electrical outlet.

What to try next

Hang a row of pictures with equal spacing between frames.

title: How to Silence a Squeaky Door Hinge
body:
Stop a door hinge from squeaking using lubricant worked into the pin.

Skill level: Beginner · Time needed: 10 minutes

Tools and materials

  • Household lubricant
  • Cloth
  • Hammer and a nail
  • Paper towel

Steps

  1. Open the door and put a cloth under the hinge to catch drips.
  2. Tap the hinge pin upward a little with the hammer and nail so it lifts slightly.
  3. Put a few drops of lubricant on the raised pin and into the hinge knuckles.
  4. Swing the door back and forth several times to work the lubricant in.
  5. Wipe off the excess with the paper towel.
  6. Repeat on the other hinges if they squeak too.

Common mistakes

  • Spraying the outside of the hinge without working the door, so the lubricant never reaches the pin.
  • Using cooking oil, which goes sticky and rancid.

Troubleshooting

  • It still squeaks: Lift the pin fully out, wipe it clean, lubricate it, and put it back.
  • Lubricant drips on the floor: Wipe it up at once and put a cloth under the hinge next time.

Safety

Doors are heavy. Prop the door so it cannot swing onto your fingers while you work.

title: How to Remove a Stripped Screw
body:
Back out a screw whose head is worn round, using grip instead of the damaged slots.

Skill level: Beginner · Time needed: 15 minutes

Tools and materials

  • Correct-size screwdriver
  • Wide rubber band
  • Pliers
  • Replacement screw

Steps

  1. Try the correct-size screwdriver first, pressing firmly while turning slowly counter-clockwise.
  2. Lay a wide rubber band flat over the screw head.
  3. Press the screwdriver through the rubber band into the head and turn slowly.
  4. If that fails, grip the edge of the screw head firmly with pliers.
  5. Turn the pliers counter-clockwise in small, steady movements.
  6. Once it is out, replace it with a new screw of the same size.

Common mistakes

  • Using the wrong size screwdriver, which strips the head further.
  • Running a power driver at full speed on a damaged head.

Troubleshooting

  • The head is completely round: Grip it with locking pliers, which hold tighter than ordinary pliers.
  • The screw will not budge: Apply penetrating oil, wait ten minutes, and try again.

Safety

Wear eye protection if you cut or file near the screw, and keep your free hand clear of the tool.

What to try next

Replace the removed screw and drive it straight with the correct bit.

title: How to Clean a Microwave Inside
body:
Use steam to loosen food splatter, then wipe the microwave clean including the turntable.

Skill level: Beginner · Time needed: 15 minutes

Tools and materials

  • Microwave-safe bowl
  • Water
  • Lemon slices or vinegar
  • Cloth
  • Sponge

Steps

  1. Fill the bowl with water and add lemon slices or a splash of vinegar.
  2. Microwave the bowl for three minutes so steam fills the cavity.
  3. Wait two minutes before opening the door so the steam can work.
  4. Wipe the ceiling, walls, and floor with the cloth.
  5. Lift out the turntable and wash it separately with warm soapy water.
  6. Dry everything, wipe the door seal, and put the turntable back.

Common mistakes

  • Scrubbing with abrasive pads, which scratch the interior.
  • Spraying cleaner into the vents, where it can damage the electronics.

Troubleshooting

  • A smell remains: Repeat with vinegar water and leave the door open for a while afterwards.
  • A stain will not lift: Apply a baking-soda paste, wait five minutes, then wipe.

Safety

The bowl and steam are hot. Use mitts and wait before opening the door to avoid a steam burn.

What to try next

Wipe the turntable weekly so splatter never bakes on.

title: How to Sharpen a Kitchen Knife with a Whetstone
body:
Restore a dull kitchen knife to a sharp, even edge using a water stone and a steady angle.

Skill level: Practised beginner · Time needed: 20 minutes

Tools and materials

  • Whetstone (1000/3000 grit or similar)
  • Water
  • Towel
  • The knife

Steps

  1. Soak the whetstone in water for about ten minutes until bubbles stop.
  2. Put the stone on a damp towel, coarse side up, so it cannot slide.
  3. Hold the knife at about fifteen to twenty degrees to the stone.
  4. Press lightly and sweep the blade from heel to tip across the stone.
  5. Do ten strokes, then flip the knife and do ten strokes on the other side.
  6. Turn the stone to the fine side and repeat with lighter pressure.
  7. Rinse the knife, dry it, and test the edge on paper or a tomato.

Common mistakes

  • Changing the angle mid-stroke, which rounds the edge instead of sharpening it.
  • Pressing too hard, which can chip the edge.
  • Using the stone dry, which clogs it with metal dust.

Troubleshooting

  • It is still dull: Check that your angle stays constant and do more strokes on the coarse side.
  • You feel a rough burr: Do light alternating strokes on the fine side until the burr is gone.

Safety

Always cut away from your body, keep fingers behind the edge, and dry your hands so the handle cannot slip.

What to try next

Hone the edge with a honing steel between full sharpenings.

title: How to Change a Watch Battery
body:
Open a watch case, swap the small battery for the exact same type, and close the case without damage.

Skill level: Practised beginner · Time needed: 20 minutes

Tools and materials

  • Small flat case tool
  • Plastic tweezers
  • Correct replacement battery
  • Soft cloth

Steps

  1. Work on a soft cloth so small parts cannot roll away or scratch.
  2. Look at the case back to see whether it screws off or snaps off.
  3. Open it carefully with the case tool, keeping the tool away from the movement.
  4. Note the battery number and which side faces up before touching it.
  5. Lift the old battery out with plastic tweezers.
  6. Put the new battery in with the same side up and press it gently into place.
  7. Close the case back fully and check that the watch runs.

Common mistakes

  • Fitting the wrong battery number, which may not work or may leak.
  • Using metal tweezers, which can short the battery.
  • Touching the battery face with bare fingers, leaving oil on it.

Troubleshooting

  • The watch still does not run: Check the battery number and orientation again.
  • You see moisture inside: Leave the watch to a professional instead of closing it up.

Safety

Small batteries are dangerous if swallowed. Keep them away from children and pets.

What to try next

Replace a watch strap using the spring-bar tool.

title: How to Use a Fire Extinguisher (PASS)
body:
Learn the four PASS steps so you can act on a small, contained fire without panic.

Skill level: Practised beginner · Time needed: 5 minutes to learn

Tools and materials

  • An ABC-type fire extinguisher
  • A clear exit route behind you

Steps

  1. Pull the pin to break the tamper seal.
  2. Aim the nozzle at the base of the fire, not at the flames.
  3. Squeeze the handle to release the agent.
  4. Sweep the nozzle from side to side across the base of the fire until it goes out.
  5. Watch for re-ignition, and keep your exit at your back the whole time.
  6. If the fire grows, produces heavy smoke, or the extinguisher empties, leave at once and call emergency services.

Common mistakes

  • Aiming at the flames instead of the base, which wastes the agent.
  • Standing too close or blocking your own exit.

Troubleshooting

  • The pin will not pull: Twist it slightly while pulling; do not force it with tools.
  • The extinguisher runs out: Leave immediately; never stay to fight a fire empty-handed.

Safety

Only tackle a fire that is small and contained, with a clear exit. If smoke fills the room, leave and call emergency services. Never re-enter a burning building.

What to try next

Check your extinguisher gauge once a month and note its expiry date.

title: How to Design and Tune a Paper Airplane
body:
Fold a paper airplane with symmetrical wings and tune it so it glides far and straight.

Skill level: Practised beginner · Time needed: 20 minutes

Tools and materials

  • A4 or letter paper
  • Flat table
  • Ruler (optional)

Steps

  1. Fold the paper in half lengthwise, crease sharply, then unfold it.
  2. Fold both top corners into the centre crease.
  3. Fold the new slanted edges into the centre crease again for a sharper nose.
  4. Fold the whole plane in half outward, away from the folds.
  5. Fold each wing down so its edge lines up with the bottom of the body.
  6. Check that both wings match exactly, then test-glide it gently.
  7. Tune it: bend the trailing edges up slightly if it nosedives, down slightly if it stalls.

Common mistakes

  • Folding one wing differently from the other, which makes the plane turn or dive.
  • Creasing the wings themselves heavily, which adds drag.

Troubleshooting

  • It nosedives: Bend the back edges of the wings up a little.
  • It stalls and drops: Bend the back edges down a little or add a small nose fold.

Safety

Never aim a paper airplane at a person or animal, and keep it away from eyes.

What to try next

Build a wide glider version and a narrow dart version and compare their flights.

title: How to Parallel Park
body:
Reverse into a street parking space between two cars, finishing straight and close to the kerb.

Skill level: Practised beginner · Time needed: 15 minutes of practice

Tools and materials

  • A car
  • A quiet street
  • Cones or markers (optional, for practice)

Steps

  1. Find a space at least one and a half times your car's length and signal your intention.
  2. Pull up alongside the car in front of the space, about sixty centimetres out, with your mirrors roughly level.
  3. Check mirrors and blind spot, then reverse slowly while turning the wheel fully toward the kerb.
  4. When your car's front door passes the rear bumper of the car ahead, straighten the wheel briefly.
  5. Continue reversing and turn the wheel the other way to swing the front in.
  6. Straighten up, centre yourself between the two cars, and check you are close to the kerb without touching it.

Common mistakes

  • Rushing the manoeuvre instead of moving slowly with pauses to check.
  • Starting too far from the parked car, which leaves you angled and far from the kerb.

Troubleshooting

  • You end up too far from the kerb: Pull out and start again rather than shuffling sideways.
  • You end up crooked: Straighten with small forward and reverse moves.

Safety

Check for pedestrians and cyclists before and during reversing. If traffic builds up behind you, abandon the attempt and move on.

What to try next

Practise reverse bay parking in an empty car park.
